title: Salman the Persian
hookLine: who left his fire-temple home searching, served Christian teachers, was enslaved, and found the Prophet ﷺ in Medina

lines: A YOUNG MAN WHO KEEPS THE FIRE.
HE HEARS PRAYER IN A CHURCH.
cards: A young man in Persia has one job: keep the fire burning. His father, a landowner, loves him so much he barely lets him out of the house, and the household fire, the one his people tend in worship, must never go out.
One day the father sends him to the fields. On the way he passes a church, hears people praying inside, and walks in. He stays until sunset.
He never reaches the fields. Today: Salman the Persian, who tells his own story.

teach.b: The account comes in Salman's own voice, in the Musnad of Ahmad and in Ibn Ishaq's life of the Prophet.
He leaves home for Syria, and attaches himself to Christian teachers, one after another, serving each until he dies. When the last of them is dying, Salman asks: who now?
The old man tells him a prophet will appear in the land of the Arabs, in a place of palm trees between two fields of black stone, and gives him signs to look for.
So he sets out with traders, who betray him and sell him as a slave.
He's sold again, to a man in a town of palm trees. Medina. He's been carried, as a slave, to the place he was looking for.
When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, arrives, Salman goes to him and watches, testing the signs one by one, and becomes a Muslim. The companions help him buy his freedom.

Later, Bukhari tells of a day the Prophet recited a verse about believers yet to come. In Pickthall's translation: "Along with others of them who have not yet joined them." Someone asked who those were.

The Prophet put his hand on Salman and said that if faith were as far away as the Pleiades, men from among these people would reach it. Salman's story isn't a straight line. Fire, church, slavery, Medina.
Muslims remember him as a seeker, and every stage counts in his telling: the home he left, the teachers who guided him, even the wrong-way road that brought him to the right town.

how: Muslims honor Salman al-Farisi as a companion of the Prophet, retell his search as a story of seeking, and remember him in the account of the trench at Medina.

o: a Christian monk who foretold a coming prophet
a Persian seeker who found the Prophet in Medina
a Persian king who sent gifts to the Prophet

games.q: Salman the Persian — tap the pairs.
p: how far faith could be, and still reached

s: Salman found Medina by following a map
he was sold as a slave and carried there, to the place his teacher described.
his last Christian teacher told him signs to look for
a prophet in a place of palms between two fields of black stone.
the Prophet put his hand on Salman when explaining a verse
about believers yet to come: men from among these people would reach faith even at the Pleiades.

games.q: you're Salman, sent to the fields by your father. on the way you hear people praying inside a church. what do you do?
o: go in, and stay until sunset.
go home and tell your father.
games.why: he went in and stayed until sunset, and that afternoon began a search that ended in Medina.

practice: Hold one question about faith, or meaning, or how to live, that you haven't settled, without answering it, the way Salman carried the old teacher's signs on the road.
Then look back at who has helped you with it so far, a book, a parent, a friend, a stranger, and let each come with thanks. If you pray, ask God to guide you; if not, let the question stay open.

wordCard.voice: Salman, the seeker who left the fire of his home, served Christian teachers, was sold as a slave, and found the Prophet in Medina. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Salman the Persian; al-Farisi means from Persia (Fars).

carryVoice: Your line: the seeker. A winding road can still arrive where it was headed. See you tomorrow.
